Hi Susan / FinCo security team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the detailed questions from InfoSec. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on the POC and security review: 

Summary of your requirements (as we understand them):
- Avoid persistent storage of PII in hosted logs by default; ability to opt-out or redact at ingestion.
- Data residency in the US (and the option for EU-only for future scope).
- Customer-managed keys (or equivalent) for encryption at rest.
- Configurable data retention policy per-route (ability to set 90-day retention and on-demand purge).
- Role-based access controls for Redwood Console and APIs (least-privilege) + auditable break-glass for support access.
- Exportable logs/audit trail for SIEM ingest and SOC2 artifacts.

Proposed next steps:
1) Dev to share technical details on encryption, retention, and logging (attached).
2) Rishi to describe RBAC and support break-glass workflow.
3) Schedule a 30-min InfoSec sync next week to validate controls + sign DPA.
4) Start a short POC (sample workload + log sample) — timeline target: week of Mar 9.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v1.pdf (draft DPA), SAML_SSO_Setup.pdf (SSO notes).

Please confirm these items and any additional must-haves. If anything above is off, flag it and I will update.

Best,

Hi all — following up with the technical details we discussed on the call. I tried to keep answers concise; happy to go deeper in the InfoSec meeting or during the POC.

1) Logging of prompts & outputs
- Default: Hosted API logs request metadata (timestamp, route, token usage, requester ID) and optionally logs full input/output for debugging if enabled.
- Controls: Per-route flags let you disable full input/output logging; you can also enable automatic redaction rules (regex-based) at ingestion to strip PII before it hits our logs.
- POC: We can provide a sample log export with redaction applied so you can verify.

2) Encryption & keys
- Data at rest: AES-256. Keys managed in AWS KMS by default.
- Customer-managed keys: Supported (bring-your-own CMK) for hosted Dedicated customers; for Private deployments you manage all keys in your KMS/HSM.

3) Data residency & deployment modes
- Hosted (default): data reside in the region you choose (we currently support us-west-2 and us-east-1 for US).
- Dedicated / Private: full VPC deployment or on-prem option to guarantee residency and network isolation.

4) Retention & deletion
- Default request payload retention: 30 days.
- Configurable: route-level retention can be set to 0 (no storage), X days (customer defined), or manual purge on request.
- Audit logs: retained 180 days by default; longer retention available as an add-on and export to your SIEM via syslog/HTTPS.

5) Support access & auditing
- RBAC: fine-grained roles (admin, dev, observer, support) with scoped permissions.
- Support access: access is granted via time-limited, least-privilege roles. Break-glass requires an explicit ticket + manager approval and generates immutable audit entries (who, why, duration, session transcript).
- We also provide session recordings and log exports for any break-glass session for your review.

6) Compliance artifacts
- We can share SOC2 attestation and our security pack (see attachment SOC2_Attestation_2025.pdf).

Next steps from my side:
- Share SAML SSO setup doc and a short checklist for Okta/JIT provisioning (attached).
- Provide a sample log export with redaction enabled for your InfoSec to review.

If you'd like, we can prepare a short config template for your engineers to review before the POC.

Cheers,

Hi Susan — quick note from a security controls perspective to clarify the RBAC and break-glass behavior.

RBAC model
- Roles: Organization Admin, Project Admin, Developer, Observer, Support (read-only or scoped write).
- Scope: Roles can be scoped to organization, project, or individual route level.
- Principle of least privilege: default onboarding creates only the minimum roles; additional privileges must be requested / approved.

Support access & break-glass
- Hosted plan: support engineers cannot unilaterally enable access to full unredacted inputs/outputs. Any elevated access request goes through our internal break-glass workflow: request via ticket, justification logged, approval required from two managers (one from product ops, one from security), access granted as a time-limited one-time token.
- All break-glass events are recorded (audit log + session transcript). The transcript and logs are exportable.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments: we support customer-managed break-glass procedures (e.g., enterprise customers may configure their own approvers via our SSO/JIT integration).

Operational controls
- Background checks and training applied to support staff on enterprise contracts.
- JIT (just-in-time) access via Okta/SCIM is supported to avoid standing privileges.

If FinCo would like, we can:
- Provide a short SOP document showing the full break-glass flow and sample audit entries.
- Set up a time-limited support session during the POC so you can validate the audit trail.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security Compliance | Redwood Inference
